homeworks.title: Lab assignment 1 - Functions and Animal class
homeworks.notes:
We will present our assignments during the lab. The teacher may require us to make changes to the code while presenting so he knows we know how to code.

For this first assignment:

1. Make two functions that
1.1 Compute the maximu element of a list of strings
1.2 Implement another operation on the list at your choice - there can not be two identical solutions
1.3 Show the execution of the two funtions on a list

2. Make a class Animal that has
2.1 Three variables: AnimalType as a string and two extra variables at your choice - there can not be two identical classes
2.2 Implement functions that put values and get values for the three variables plus the constructor
2.3 Implement two extra operations on the variables - two choices can not be identical
2.4 Show the execution of the functions on two objects

homeworks.subject: CSW Lab
homeworks.title: Ontologies and Jena
homeworks.notes:
1) Create in Protege an ontology regarding School that includes:

- Teachers, Students and Other Staff as categories

- Include 4-5 types of Teachers

- Include 2-3 types of OtherStaff

- Include 5 Individual as Teachers, 4 as Students and 3 as Subcategories of OtherStaff

- 2 Relations between Classes

- 10 Data Properties

Note: There can not be two identical Ontologies

Save it as an RDF



2) In NetBeans, Jena read the ontology, display its statements and display all the predicates of the individuals that you create



3) Create via programing an ontology in a similar fashion as we created "mates" at laboratory. You need to create a class regarding animals with 6 property like name, species, etc. Save it

4) Merge the two ontologies: one from Protege and one from programing.

5) List all the statements of the new ontology.

homeworks.subject: CSW Lab
homeworks.title: NLP + Classifiers
homeworks.notes:
I. NLP part
*****
For this assignment you will do the followings
1. Select 
  - 3 texts related to depression from Internet and save it in three separate files
  - 3 texts from Internet from different posts of persons and save it in three separate files
2. For each of the 6 files from above do the folowing:
   - split the text in sentences
   - split the sentences in words
   - Remove punctuation
   - Remove stop-words
   - do the stemming 
   - Compute the frequencies of the stems
   - Save the frequencies in a list of pairs (stem, frequency)
   - Compute the first 20 top frequencies from   list of pairs and save it in a new list
   - Print the new list
   
II. Clasifiers part
******""
I. With the words frequencies from the previous assignment, for the 6 files (3 depressed, 3 non-depressed) prepare a CVS file (input.txt) with the following format
Category  Label word1 word 2 ....
1      depressed 0.3 0.4 ..
0 non-depressed 0.5 067..
....
Notes:
1) word1 word2 ... are the words that comes from the union of the first 5 words from each file from the 6
2) numbers in the example (0.3, 0.4...) are just to show an example. You need to put the real numbers from the frequencies of the words that are coming from the python code from the previous assignment  from the run from the  6 files
II. Modify the code from classifiers laboratory to run on the new file input.txt and to classify the 6 files as coming from depressed and non-depressed persons

homeworks.subject: ATCN
homeworks.title: Install virtual machines (Vagrant)
homeworks.notes:
If anything is unclear, check the ATCN moodle.

Thanks to Mihai for describing the steps:

To install the virtual machines using the script
- make a directory on your pc
- throw the file in there from moodle
- command prompt/bash/etc. navigate to folder and run the command mentioned ( probably "vagrant init", it is probably mentioned in course 4)
- the scrip will install the virtual machines for you
- each vm is about 1gb
- it will create 2 machines at the same time
- if you change parameters you can create a different number of virtual machines( not recommended if you don't know what you are doing )
- it will be ubuntu
- at the end is should say smth like "ssh successfull" or "machine create successfully", around there, and then return to command prompt
- if that does not happen wait for a couple of minutes
- if it still doesnt succed/appears frozen stop it, might have been a missmatch between vagrant and vm
- then uninstall everything and look for a different versions or vagrant and vm
- each machine is set at 1gb of ram( check parameters ) and 1 core
- after everything is installed run in cmd "vagrant halt" to shut down the machines so they dont use resources ( they will remain installed, it's just like shutting down your computer, but you shut down the vm's)
- use "vagrant up" to start the vm's
